components.name: Primary Button (Amber)
components.description: The one amber 'safelight' primary action. Warm-white label at ~3:1 (AA large) — semibold button label only; for small text on amber use olive or dark text.

components.name: Image Grid Tile (selected)
components.description: Signature component. Uniform tile with designed hover / selected / focus states; selected shows the amber active wash + the brighter amber-glow active bar.
components.css: .ds-tile { position:relative; width:160px; height:160px; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid #d8d3c8; overflow:hidden; cursor:pointer; transition:box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 150ms; } .ds-tile-photo { position:absolute; inset:0; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#8a94a3,#5f6b7a); } .ds-tile:hover { box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(28,22,12,0.18); } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(196,122,30,0.55); } .ds-tile--selected { box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 9999px rgba(196,122,30,0.20); } .ds-tile--selected::after { content:""; position:absolute; left:0; top:0; bottom:0; width:3px; background:#e08a2a; } .ds-tile-badge { position:absolute; left:6px; bottom:6px; background:rgba(255,255,255,0.55); color:#23211d; font:600 0.6875rem system-ui,sans-serif; padding:2px 6px; border-radius:4px; backdrop-filter:blur(2px); }

narrative.overview: PixlStash is a self-hosted library where people who generate AI images at volume triage, score, and organize thousands of frames. The screen is mostly a dense grid of the user's own pictures, so the design works like a darkroom: the chrome dims to a warm safelight and the photos are the only thing that glows. The single amber accent is the safelight — used on the primary action and the key state, and almost nowhere else. The system is warm, quiet, and pixel-honest: warm neutrals (never cold grey or pure black/white), one amber accent spent sparingly, and a pixel-art padlock + Tiny5 pixel face that appear only in brand moments, never in working UI. The palette is unified across both themes — the four brand hues and four status colors are a single value shared by dark and light, each deep enough to carry the warm-white label; only the neutrals switch. Both themes are first-class and every decision must hold in both, but the design is led from dark, where volume review actually happens.
keyCharacteristics: The photos are the color; the chrome is a warm, dim frame around them.
One amber accent, spent sparingly, on primary action and key state.
Warm neutrals only — near-black on near-white, never cold grey or pure black/white.
Dense by design (14px base), but density is earned by the grid, not the controls.
Polish lives in designed focus / hover / selected / empty / loading states.
Every value comes from a token; a new value is a design decision, not an inline tweak.

rules.name: The One Safelight Rule
rules.body: Amber marks intent, not decoration. One amber action per view, ≤~10% of a screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Unified-Palette Rule
rules.body: Brand and status colors are the same hex in both themes; only neutrals flip. A theme-specific brand color is drift.

rules.name: The Warm-White-Label Rule
rules.body: Text on any deep brand/status fill is the warm-white on-fill (#f7f1ea), never pure #fff. The one exception is Warning, whose bright orange takes dark text (#1b1b1b) — the hazard convention.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Color-Alone Rule
rules.body: Error/warning/success/info always pair color with an icon or text; color never carries meaning by itself, and status colors never appear as decoration.

rules.name: The Categorizers-Label-Not-Act Rule
rules.body: Raspberry and teal identify and group; they never sit on a button.

rules.name: The No-Hex Rule
rules.body: A hex literal in a component is drift. Every color is a token; if the color you want isn't one, you want the nearest one.

rules.name: The Warmth Rule
rules.body: Never cold grey, never pure #000/#fff; text, canvas, borders, and shadows all stay warm.

rules.name: The rem-Only Rule
rules.body: Size type in rem, from the ramp. Never em (it compounds with its parent and is the main reason nested labels drift), never a raw px one-off. This is the single biggest typographic drift to hold the line on.

rules.name: The 600-Not-700 Rule
rules.body: Headings are weight 600. 700 reads heavy against the warm near-black and is reserved for rare true emphasis. Hierarchy comes from weight, color, and space at least as much as from size.

rules.name: The Tiny5-Is-Brand-Only Rule
rules.body: The pixel face never sets a label, button, menu item, or any reading text — it is gorgeous as a mark and illegible as body. Brand moments only.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is built on --v-theme-shadow. Never hardcode a shadow color; a cold shadow on a warm canvas is an instant tell.

rules.name: The Dark-Leans-On-Lightness Rule
rules.body: In dark mode, convey elevation by making the surface lighter, not by stacking a heavier shadow (which just muddies).

rules.name: The Consistent-Radius Rule
rules.body: Radii stay consistent within a component family. An 8px card with a 4px button inside it is correct; an 8px card beside a 6px sibling card is drift.

dos: Do reach for a token before typing a value — color as rgb(var(--v-theme-*)), everything else from --space-* / --radius-* / --text-* / --elevation-* / --dur-*. A genuinely new value is a design decision, raised with the lead designer, not an inline tweak.
Do size type from the ramp, in rem, at 14px base; headings at weight 600.
Do design focus, hover, selected, empty, and loading states for anything interactive — that is where polish lives.
Do validate both themes on every change, and lead from dark since that is where review happens; keep light fully first-class.
Do align to the grid and to the 48px shell band — same row shares a baseline, columns share a left edge.
Do use --focus-ring on every focusable element; keyboard flow is a product requirement here, not a nicety.
donts: Don't hardcode a hex color, a rgba(0,0,0,…) shadow/scrim, or an off-grid size/radius — those are exactly the size/alignment/color drift to eliminate.
Don't size text in em, or introduce a point size outside the ramp.
Don't set UI, labels, or body text in Tiny5 — brand moments only — and don't reintroduce PressStart2P.
Don't spend the amber accent broadly; one safelight, used sparingly.
Don't pull in a second icon set — Material Design Icons only in the chrome.
Don't let chrome compete with the photos; when in doubt, make the chrome quieter.
